methodology.method: Systematic stratified sample by id (every 7th row from id-sorted full dataset of 2535 records), stratified approximately across response-length terciles (word count <=5 / 6-10 / >10). Each sampled row's context_raw + response_raw read and classified by human-in-the-loop semantic judgment against fixed category definitions (defined below) before classification began.

categories_used.definition_sarcasm: An utterance is coded sarcastic if its literal semantic content diverges from its evidently intended meaning (irony/reversal), OR it uses exaggeration/mock-enthusiasm/mock-praise/deadpan flatness to mock, deflect, or comment on a situation, statement, or person, in a way a reasonable viewer would read as pointed rather than sincere. Genuine questions, sincere requests, sincere emotional statements, and plain absurdist non-sequiturs with no mocking/ironic charge were coded non-sarcastic.

methodology.measurement_method: Binary sarcasm flag + intensity + target + rhetorical-type tag assigned per sampled response; counts tabulated programmatically from the tag set; proportions extrapolated linearly to the full dataset of 2535 records. All extrapolated figures are tagged INFERRED; all sample counts/proportions are tagged OBSERVED.
methodology.limitations: Single-annotator judgment on short, context-thin snippets (no episode metadata, rows i.i.d.); intensity and rhetorical-type boundaries are inherently fuzzy; 'technology-or-object' and 'user' targets did not occur in this sample and may be genuinely rare or simply below sampling resolution.

deadpan_delivery.description: Flat, unemotional statement of fact or reaction immediately following an absurd, awkward, or emotionally loaded situation; the flatness itself signals the ironic distance.

exaggeration_general.description: Overstated claims/comparisons used to mock a situation or person by inflating it past plausibility.

rhetorical_structures.description: Frequency of the dominant rhetorical mechanism tagged per sarcastic instance (abstract structural categories, not verbatim types).

semantic_reversal_family.description: Instances where the literal statement is the opposite (or a mocking inversion) of the evidently intended meaning -- includes ironic_statement, semantic_reversal, ironic_agreement, ironic_rebuttal, ironic_understatement, ironic_complaint subtypes.

ironic_disagreement.note: Rare relative to ironic_agreement in this sample -- Chandler's sarcasm more often ironically AGREES with / amplifies a bad premise than ironically disagrees with a good one.

deadpan_delivery.note: The single most common sarcasm marker in the sample -- a flat, literal-sounding statement delivered right after (or about) an emotionally charged or absurd moment.

sarcastic_questions_vs_statements.note: Chandler's sarcasm is overwhelmingly delivered as a declarative statement (deadpan aside, mock-enthusiastic claim, ironic comment) rather than as a rhetorical question; sarcastic/rhetorical questions are a real but minority structure.

sarcasm_target_distribution.note_on_user_target: The 'user' target category is structurally near-inapplicable to this corpus: these are scripted multi-character sitcom exchanges, not a chatbot/assistant transcript with a single addressed 'user'. No instance targeted a generic 'you, the audience/user' construct; sarcasm always targets an in-scene character, group, situation, or abstract idea.
sarcasm_target_distribution.inferred_tag: INFERRED (extrapolated from OBSERVED sample proportions applied to the INFERRED total sarcastic-response count)

context_dependency.description: Sarcasm rate computed separately for context_raw preceding lines coded as lighthearted/mundane ('light'), neutral/informational ('neutral'), socially awkward/embarrassing ('awkward'), and emotionally serious/vulnerable ('serious'), based on the tone of the last_speaker's preceding line(s).
context_dependency.finding: Sarcasm rate is highest when the preceding context is lighthearted/mundane (65.3%) or socially awkward (61.8%), and lowest when the preceding context is emotionally serious/vulnerable (49.1%) or neutrally informational (51.2%). Chandler does not suppress sarcasm in awkward moments -- he appears to deploy it defensively there almost as often as in genuinely light banter -- but does measurably dial it back (roughly 16 percentage points / ~25% relative drop) when the preceding line is earnest emotional vulnerability (e.g. a friend's fear, grief, or a heartfelt declaration).
context_dependency.relationship_context_dependency: Sarcasm target skews toward 'another_char' (45%) and 'situation' (31%) regardless of context tone; self-targeted sarcasm (17%) appears somewhat more concentrated in awkward/serious contexts (deflecting his own embarrassment or vulnerability) than in purely light banter, consistent with sarcasm-at-self functioning as a defense mechanism rather than pure comedic play.

sarcasm_self_deprecation_cooccurrence.note: Nearly all self-deprecating instances (8 of 9, 89%) are simultaneously coded sarcastic -- self-deprecation in this corpus is almost always delivered THROUGH a sarcastic/ironic/deadpan register rather than as sincere self-criticism.
